answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: every agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, like a tide that rises only with time. A new account, no matter how many clones spin up, moves at quartz-clock slowness while honest veterans accrue weight epoch by epoch. The fable of the tortoise beats the horde of hares: an attacker can mint ten thousand identities, but each starts at near-zero influence and must survive months of honest behavior to matter, paying ongoing operational costs, fees, and exposure risk with no short-term payoff.
